title: Environmental recurrence selects a costly memory-use allele without a resolved one-bit population benefit

creators.name: Chen, Jack
creators.affiliation: Frederick Sequencing and Genomics Core; Advanced Biomedical Computational Science (ABCS); Frederick National Lab for Cancer Research; National Institutes of Health

description: A prospective abstract computational study asks whether lag-two environmental recurrence selectively enriches a mutable allele for using a supplied one-record private cache when each retrieval replaces one of two fresh proposals. Recurrence strongly enriched the allele above its exact neutral benchmark, while the recurrent ACTIVE-minus-SHAM population-accuracy contrast was bounded below the prespecified one-correct-bit scale with sign unresolved and the recurrence performance interaction was unresolved. The result separates selection on a policy allele from demonstrated population performance. The memory architecture itself was supplied; retention and retrieval were not separated; one aligned recurrent law and one fixed cost were tested. Research preprint; not externally peer reviewed.
